newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS WINS THIRD-STRAIGHT AMATEUR TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS WINS THIRD-STRAIGHT AMATEUR TITLE.

text.p: Tiger Woods defeated Steve Scott on the second hole of a sudden-death playoff for a record third consecutive U.S. Amateur Golf Championship on Sunday.

Woods never led until sinking a short par putt after Scott had missed a seven-footer on the 10th hole -- the 38th of the day and 164th of the week-long tournament. Woods trailed by as many as five holes in the 36-hole match-play final and by two holes with just three to play.

Woods became the first golfer to win the U.S. Amateur title in three straight years. He also won U.S. Junior Amateurs in 1991, 1992 and 1993 and joined the legendary Bobby Jones as the only golfers to win USGA events in six straight years. Jones won the U.S. Amateur or U.S. Open in every year from 1923 to 1930.
With nearly no margin for error, Woods birdied the 16th and 17th holes, rolling in a 30-foot putt on 17 to square the match.

After both players parred the first playoff hole, Woods hit a six-iron on the 204-yard 10th hole within eight feet of the cup. Scott missed the green and rolled his chip attempt past the hole. Woods missed badly on his birdie, but Scott lipped his par putt. The 20-year-old Woods tapped in for the gut-wrenching win.

Woods receives automatic entry into next year's Masters and U.S. Open, if he is still an amateur. The Stanford student intends to play in next week's Greater Milwaukee Open as an amateur and has said he will turn pro if he wins the event.

Woods defeated Stanford University teammate Joel Kribel, 3 and 1, in Saturday's semifinals. Scott posted a 3 and 2 victory over Robert Floyd, the son of Senior PGA Tour mainstay Raymond Floyd, in a battle of University of Florida teammates.
